# Figures 5 and 6, and the extrastriate supplement, under the settled specification

**Generated by [`cleanroom/run_spec_outputs.m`](cleanroom/run_spec_outputs.m)** — one command,
two to three minutes. Everything below is regenerable; nothing was transcribed by hand.

**Three variants**, because route and weighting are orthogonal knobs and the comparison is only
readable if they change one at a time ([`cleanroom/spec_variants.m`](cleanroom/spec_variants.m)):

| tag | route | weighting | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`spec`** | harmonic model, continuous θ_V | equal | **primary** — the settled specification |
| `roi` | eight polar-angle wedges | equal | `spec` vs `roi` isolates the **route** |
| `roipw` | eight polar-angle wedges | precision | `roi` vs `roipw` isolates the **weighting** |

There is deliberately no harmonic-plus-precision variant: adding it would leave no pair differing
in exactly one thing. Every figure in every variant is drawn on **one set of axis limits computed
across all three**, so they can be laid side by side.

This document says what was produced, how it differs from the previous figures, and what the
numbers changed. The specification itself is [`EXTRASTRIATE.md`](EXTRASTRIATE.md) §1 and is not
restated here.

Every table carries `variant`, `route` and `weighting` columns, and both the equal-weighted
(`eq_*`) and precision-weighted (`pw_*`) estimates in every row, whichever the variant made
primary. Reporting only one would hide that the choice is a choice.

## How Figures 5 and 6 changed

**Row 1 (polar plots)** now carries **two things**: lines are the fitted four-term harmonic model,
markers are the observed wedge means over the same vertices. Where they separate — visibly in the
radial/tangential and polar-cardinal panels — the gap *is* the within-wedge local-orientation term
that binning θV conflates with context ([`HARMONIC_MODEL.md`](HARMONIC_MODEL.md) Result 1). It is
now shown rather than argued.

**The radius is demeaned.** The model is fitted to each vertex's four orientation responses with
that vertex's mean over the four removed, so it carries no overall response level: the radial axis
is a deviation from the local mean, not a raw percent signal change. That is deliberate — demeaning
removes the blank, which is full-field pink noise rather than a baseline
([`local_qc/REPORT.md`](local_qc/REPORT.md) §1), so only orientation *differences* enter.

**Row 2 is no longer the pro-vs-con paired plot.** Under this parameterisation the two classes are
demeaned and partition the four orientations, so `con = −pro` exactly for the two second-harmonic
asymmetries and the paired plot would show the same information mirrored. Each observer's
**difference** is plotted instead, with the group mean and its interval — the difference is the
estimand, so the difference is what is shown.

**Intervals are *t* on n−1 df, not the percentile bootstrap.** See "the interval question" below.

### Axis scales are shared, and shared across both figures

Panels drawn in the same units showing the same kind of comparison are on one scale.
Otherwise a small effect on a small axis looks like a large one, and the reader has to check
tick labels to avoid being misled — which is what a figure is meant to save them from.

| panels | scale | why |
|---|---|---|
| every polar panel, **Figures 5 and 6 together** | ±0.62 | same units, same comparison |
| every difference panel, **Figures 5 and 6 together** | [−0.79, 0.38] | same |
| all six profile panels | [−1.10, 0.58] | all are pro-minus-con orientation contrasts |
| hierarchy figure, top row | [−0.70, 0.30] | four asymmetries |
| hierarchy figure, bottom row | [−0.55, 0.15] | four context effects — a *different* quantity, so not linked to the row above |

The limits deliberately span **both experiments**, so Figure 5 and Figure 6 are comparable to each
other rather than merely internally consistent. `dg`-versus-`da` is the paper's claim; drawing the
two on different scales would undercut the one comparison a reader most needs to make by eye. One
definition, in [`cleanroom/spec_axis_limits.m`](cleanroom/spec_axis_limits.m).

A consequence worth stating: on the shared profile scale the two second-harmonic panels are small.
That is the finding, not a drawing problem — `card−obl` and `polc−polo` *are* about a quarter the
size of the first-harmonic contrasts, and the previous per-panel autoscaling concealed it.

### Why the polar plots stay at 45° and are not binned at 15°

Asked and settled 2026-08-24. **The pro/con classes only exist at multiples of 45° for half the
panels**, because a class is defined by an exact match on local orientation or on offset from the
pRF angle:

- **`dg`** — stimulus orientation is fixed, so *horizontal* and *cardinal* are the same classes at
  every polar angle and panels A/B could be binned arbitrarily finely. But *radial* means offset
  `d = 0`, and at θ_V = 15° the four offsets are 165°/75°/30°/120°: **no stimulus is radial**.
  Panels C and D have nothing to average.
- **`da`** — the mirror image. The stimulus rotates with polar angle, so pinwheel is radial and
  annulus tangential everywhere and panels C/D bin finely; but at θ_V = 15° the local orientations
  are 15°/105°/60°/150°, so nothing is horizontal or vertical and panels A/B do not.

Binning finely would therefore produce a figure with 24 markers in four panels and 8 in the other
four — the same inconsistency the shared scales exist to remove. And the fine version already
exists: **`Figure_5_6_spec_profile` is the 15°-binned version of exactly the four panels that
permit it**, which is why it has three columns rather than four. The eight wedges are also the units
the asymmetry is defined over, since the specification reads the coefficients off at the eight
canonical ROI centres.

### `Figure_5_6_spec_profile` — the new one

Three panels per experiment: the only three orientation contrasts **measurable at a single polar
angle**. Four orientations at 45° spacing give each vertex's demeaned response exactly three degrees
of freedom, so a profile against continuous θV can show three curves and no more. The fourth
coefficient is identified *across* vertices, from the θV modulation of the first and third — which
is what the tilt of these curves is.

This is the figure that shows why θV is continuous rather than binned. Binning would replace each
curve with eight points and put `cos(4θV)` at only two values, which is exactly degenerate once one
ROI class is lost ([`EXTRASTRIATE.md`](EXTRASTRIATE.md) §5).

The model tracks the data across the full 360° in all six panels. As an internal check, the mean of
the fitted profile over polar angle equals the reported asymmetry to machine precision.

## What the numbers did — V1, 4–8°

The previous figures used the ROI route (θV at the wedge centre); the specification uses continuous
θV. Same vertices, same gain, same weighting — **only θV differs**, so the column headed *delta* is
exactly the within-wedge geometry term.

| exp | asymmetry | ROI route | specification | delta |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| dg | horiz−vert | −0.548 | −0.548 | +0.000 |
| dg | card−obl | −0.221 | −0.221 | −0.001 |
| dg | rad−tang | 0.104 | **0.119** | +0.015 |
| dg | polc−polo | 0.039 | **0.072** | +0.033 |
| da | horiz−vert | −0.218 | −0.232 | −0.013 |
| da | card−obl | −0.028 | −0.041 | −0.012 |
| da | rad−tang | 0.150 | 0.155 | +0.005 |
| da | polc−polo | 0.040 | 0.033 | −0.007 |

**Maximum movement 0.033, and no asymmetry changes significance.** The two that move are `dg`
rad−tang and `dg` polc−polo — the terms that depend on θV in the Cartesian experiment, which is
where the geometry correction has to land. For `dg` the `cos(2θ)` and `cos(4θ)` columns are
vertex-independent, so the first two rows cannot move and do not.

Context effects (dg − da), paired within observer:

| asymmetry | ROI route | specification | delta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| horiz−vert | −0.330 | −0.316 | +0.014 |
| card−obl | −0.192 | −0.181 | +0.012 |
| rad−tang | −0.046 | −0.036 | +0.010 |
| polc−polo | −0.001 | **+0.039** | +0.040 |

The polc−polo context effect moves most, from essentially zero to +0.039, and remains
non-significant (*p* = .354) either way.

## What the alternative routes change

Same vertices, same gain, same observers throughout — only the named thing differs.

**The route** (`spec` → `roi`, both equal-weighted). V1, 4–8°:

| exp | asymmetry | spec | roi | delta |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| dg | horiz−vert | −0.548 | −0.548 | 0.000 |
| dg | card−obl | −0.221 | −0.221 | 0.000 |
| dg | rad−tang | 0.119 | 0.104 | −0.015 |
| dg | polc−polo | 0.072 | 0.039 | −0.033 |
| da | horiz−vert | −0.232 | −0.218 | +0.014 |
| da | card−obl | −0.041 | −0.028 | +0.013 |
| da | rad−tang | 0.155 | 0.150 | −0.005 |
| da | polc−polo | 0.033 | 0.040 | +0.007 |

Context effects: horiz−vert −0.316 → −0.330, card−obl −0.181 → −0.192, rad−tang −0.036 → −0.046,
polc−polo **+0.039 → −0.001**. **No cell changes significance.** The two Cartesian `dg` rows are
identical to three decimals because their regressors are θ_V-free, so the route cannot touch them;
everything that moves is a term that depends on θ_V, which is where a binning difference has to land.

**The weighting** (`roi` → `roipw`). The estimates barely move — largest change 0.025, on `da`
rad−tang (0.150 → 0.175, *p* .041 → .007). Every context effect is unchanged to within 0.015, and
again **no cell changes significance**. That is the result `LME.md` §5 predicts: τ² is common to
every observer and here exceeds the mean σᵢ², so a 14× spread in *reliability* compresses into a
~3× spread in *weight*.

**The hierarchy trend is unaffected by either.** V1 − V3, within observer:

| | horiz−vert | card−obl |
|---|---|---|
| `spec` | −0.215, *p* = .028 | −0.066, *p* = .153 |
| `roi` | −0.221, *p* = .030 | −0.084, *p* = .060 |

Same conclusion under both: the decline is established for horizontal−vertical and not for
cardinal−oblique. The trend is **always equal-weighted**, whatever variant is requested, so the
`roi` and `roipw` trend tables are byte-identical — asserted, not assumed. Precision weighting it
would need the within-observer covariance of one observer's estimate in two different maps, and
those come from the same runs, so their errors are correlated by an unmeasured amount; assuming
independence would understate the SE.

**What the ROI figures look like.** The polar plots lose the model overlay — that route fits no
per-vertex model, so the lines simply join the wedge means. In the profile figure the curve becomes
a **step function**: the wedge means held constant across each 45° wedge, which is exactly what the
ROI route assumes about polar-angle structure. Drawn against the same 15° data it shows what the
assumption costs — most visibly in `radial − tangential`, where the steps cannot follow the peaks.

**Bottom line.** Neither the route nor the weighting changes any conclusion in V1. The
specification is preferable for the reasons in [`EXTRASTRIATE.md`](EXTRASTRIATE.md) §2–§5 — chiefly
that the ROI route degrades where cells go empty, which is the extrastriate case, not this one.

## The interval question, partly resolved

[`LME.md`](LME.md) §7 recorded that the percentile bootstrap and the *t* interval disagree on **two**
polar cells, and that this needed a decision before submission. Under the specification **only one
still disagrees**:

| cell | mean | *t* 95% CI | *p* | bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|--:|---|--:|---|
| `da` card−obl | −0.041 | [−0.092, 0.011] | .105 | [−0.083, −0.002] |
| `da` rad−tang | 0.155 | [0.023, 0.287] | .028 | [0.043, 0.243] |

`da` rad−tang now agrees — both intervals exclude zero — because the specification's gain rescaling
tightened it. `da` card−obl still disagrees, and the honest reading is the *t* one: *p* = .105, not
significant. Both columns are in `spec_asymmetries_v1_4-8.csv` with a `ci_methods_disagree` flag, so
the choice stays visible rather than being made silently.

*t* is primary throughout, because at n = 8 the percentile bootstrap has poor coverage and does not
account for uncertainty in the spread.

## The extrastriate supplement

### Coverage, and which maps qualify

Evaluated rather than assumed, on the [`EXTRASTRIATE.md`](EXTRASTRIATE.md) §6 criterion: at most 2
empty (observer × ROI) cells of 64, a median of at least 20 vertices per cell, a maximum
precision-weight ratio below 25, and a per-map gain that exists.

| map | band | empty/64 | median vertices/cell | max weight ratio | reportable |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| V1 | 4–8° | 0 | 150.5 | 17.1 | **yes** |
| V1 | 2–10° | 0 | 326.5 | 18.1 | **yes** |
| V2 | 4–8° | 0 | 136 | 15.8 | **yes** |
| V2 | 2–10° | 0 | 325 | 8.6 | **yes** |
| V3 | 4–8° | 1 | 80 | 10.3 | **yes** |
| V3 | 2–10° | 0 | 202.5 | 10.1 | **yes** |
| V3a | 4–8° | 4 | 18.5 | 15.4 | no |
| V3a | 2–10° | 1 | 44.5 | 9.5 | **yes** |
| V3b | 4–8° | 18 | 10 | 170.2 | no |
| V3b | 2–10° | 10 | 24.5 | 176.9 | no |
| hV4 | 4–8° | 24 | 4 | 22.2 | no |
| hV4 | 2–10° | 10 | 34.5 | 8.8 | no |
| MT | 4–8° | 30 | 1 | — | no |
| MT | 2–10° | 19 | 9 | 48.2 | no |
| MST | 4–8° | 28 | 1.5 | 146.8 | no |
| MST | 2–10° | 21 | 9 | 123.6 | no |

Identical to the counts already in `EXTRASTRIATE.md` §6, now regenerated from the same code path
that produces the estimates. Failing the criterion says **this design cannot resolve that map by
polar angle** — not that the map has no asymmetries. Every excluded number is still in
`spec_areas_*.csv` behind a `reportable` flag.

One addition to the criterion: **a per-map gain must exist**. MT and MST lack one for some
observers, and scoring them with a V1-derived scalar would reintroduce exactly the V1
special-casing the specification removed ([`EXTRASTRIATE.md`](EXTRASTRIATE.md) §3). They fail on
coverage anyway, so this changes no map's status; it is recorded so it cannot silently matter later.

`MT` at 4–8° has a median of **one** vertex per cell and one observer with no surviving vertices at
all, so its estimates are NaN by construction. That NaN convention — if any observer is missing,
the whole summary is NaN rather than an estimate over the observers that remain — is shared with
`precision_weighted_table.m` and is asserted to match.

### The hierarchy trend — computed, and it does not say what was assumed

[`EXTRASTRIATE.md`](EXTRASTRIATE.md) §8 recorded that the monotonic V1 → V2 → V3 decline rested on
six individually significant cells falling in the same order, and that **the trend itself had never
been computed**. It is computed here, *within observer*: for each observer, the difference of the
context effect between two maps, then a *t* test across the 8. Same observers in both maps, so the
pairing is exact and the between-observer variance that limits everything else cancels.

| comparison | asymmetry | mean | *t* 95% CI | *p* | obs |
|---|---|--:|---|--:|--:|
| V1 − V2 | horiz−vert | −0.056 | [−0.211, 0.099] | .422 | 5/8 |
| V1 − V2 | card−obl | −0.019 | [−0.092, 0.053] | .547 | 5/8 |
| V2 − V3 | horiz−vert | **−0.159** | [−0.256, −0.061] | **.006** | 8/8 |
| V2 − V3 | card−obl | −0.046 | [−0.092, −0.001] | .047 | 6/8 |
| V2 − V3 | rad−tang | 0.105 | [0.008, 0.202] | .037 | 7/8 |
| **V1 − V3** | **horiz−vert** | **−0.215** | [−0.398, −0.031] | **.028** | 7/8 |
| **V1 − V3** | **card−obl** | −0.066 | [−0.162, 0.031] | **.153** | 5/8 |

(The four polc−polo rows and the two remaining rad−tang rows are all *p* > .3; the full twelve are
in `spec_areas_trend.csv`.)

**What this establishes.** The context effect on **horizontal−vertical** genuinely attenuates from
V1 to V3: −0.215, *p* = .028, with 7 of 8 observers in the same direction, and the V2 → V3 step
carries most of it (*p* = .006, 8/8).

**What it does not.** For **cardinal−oblique** the V1 − V3 trend is **not significant** (−0.066,
*p* = .153). Only the V2 − V3 step reaches *p* = .047, which is one of twelve uncorrected tests and
should not be leaned on. So `EXTRASTRIATE.md` §7's "both Cartesian effects decline monotonically up
the hierarchy" is **established for one of the two, not both** — which is exactly the kind of thing
an untested trend hides. The individual cells are each significant in each map and do fall in
order; the *difference* between maps is only resolved for horiz−vert.

**Multiplicity.** Twelve trend tests, uncorrected. The horiz−vert results survive comfortably; the
card−obl V2 − V3 cell does not.

## How to regenerate

```bash
matlab -batch "cd('Reproduction/cleanroom'); run_spec_outputs"
```

Needs `~/dg_collect/` (the run-wise betas and the per-map gain) — see
[`server_extract/README.md`](server_extract/README.md). It does not touch
`Support/allsubjectsTable.csv`.

**Where the time goes**, measured: the 500-resample bootstrap over runs inside
`diagnose_within_observer_error`, which measures each observer's within-observer σ. It is ~75% of
every call — 4.7 s per map × band in V1, against 1.2 s at `nBoot = 50`. File I/O is negligible
(0.69 s for a pass over all 16 runbetas files), and the harmonic fit itself is ~2.7 s. `nBoot` is
the only real lever, and lowering it degrades σ, which is exactly what the precision weighting
rests on — so it is left at 500.

Individual pieces are callable without the full sweep: `spec_profiles('area','V2')`,
`spec_tables('area','V2','variant','roi')`, `spec_areas_summary('variant','roi')`.

## Code

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `cleanroom/spec_profiles.m` | fits the specification per observer; returns the model and observed profiles Figures 5/6 need |
| `cleanroom/spec_tables.m` | the V1 tables, four interval methods |
| `cleanroom/spec_areas_summary.m` | the eight-map sweep, coverage, reportability, hierarchy trend |
| `cleanroom/plot_fig5_6_spec.m` | Figures 5 and 6 |
| `cleanroom/plot_spec_profile.m` | the polar-angle profile figure |
| `cleanroom/plot_spec_hierarchy.m` | the extrastriate figure |
| `cleanroom/spec_variants.m` | the three variants and what each isolates |
| `cleanroom/spec_group.m` | the group estimator, equal or precision — **one** definition |
| `cleanroom/spec_axis_limits.m` | the shared axis limits — **one** definition, spanning all variants |
| `cleanroom/load_runbetas_area.m` | the analysed vertex set — **one** definition, shared with `diagnose_within_observer_error.m` |
| `cleanroom/run_spec_outputs.m` | the driver |

**Two guards keep the figures and the tables from drifting apart.** `spec_profiles` asserts that its
per-observer asymmetries equal the ones `diagnose_within_observer_error` computes (agreement 3e-16
in V1), and `spec_tables` asserts that its equal-weighted means equal `precision_weighted_table`'s.
Both fire on any mismatch rather than reporting two versions of the same number.

## What has not been done

- **The 2–10° band is computed but not used for the main figures.** Figures 5/6 are V1 4–8°, the
  band where spatial frequency is matched between the experiments. The 2–10° numbers are in the
  CSVs, and V3a is reportable only there.
- **Figure 8 is untouched.** Its red curve is the Fig-7 LME, which is being removed; what replaces
  it is still open (`../AGENTS.md` §7).
- **The whole-ROI analyses of hV4 and MT are unaffected** and were not rerun. The coverage criterion
  is about polar-angle resolution only.
